text:
I think for many people canceling a gym membership is something they really struggle with. They feel like they're failing. I have this mindset of not canceling gym memberships, just to prove to myself that I am going to be this disciplined person. And if I cancel it, it means I failed. But I don't know, I actually think that sometimes canceling a gym membership can be very healthy. If you're not really going there and you have other things in life, maybe the gym doesn't fit right now. Maybe it's not the right environment for you, or the right exercise. Or maybe you don't have the money. But if you really evaluate it, I think that's a good thing. If you don't really go, and you have that guilt every single month, maybe just cancel it.
Money is always a good argument. Like, 50 bucks a month, it doesn't seem like much, but if you keep that for 5 years, 10 years, it's a lot of money. And if you go once or twice a month, it's really expensive. Compared to buying some sneakers, some resistance bands, or some kind of class, community class, it's expensive. So, if you can use that money to pay your debt or invest or pay for something you actually love, I think it's a very good choice. But if you go every day and you really enjoy it, I would say gym is a good deal. They have a lot of things and people that you can't replicate at home. If you cancel a cheap gym and go to a very expensive class or buy all the equipment for your home gym, you will pay more. So money is a very good argument.
And then you also have this motivation factor that is very important. Going to a gym means you need to leave your home, go somewhere, maybe talk to people, or see people that you see every day. And that can really help. And then people say, look, if I really need discipline, I can do it myself. And I think that's true. But then, sometimes we need a framework. Sometimes we need a gym just to be able to push ourselves to move. And it's very nice to be in a social environment where people see you, where people are doing exercise. I think it really helps people keep going. But on the other hand, sometimes it's like people pay the gym to have the illusion that they are healthy. So they pay the fee but they don't actually exercise. And that can be very bad. And sometimes we go to a gym only to justify paying for it, and it becomes very punitive. Like, I really don't want to go, I have to go, I really hate it. And that's not healthy. So if you're able to exercise every day outside, or at home, or cycling, swimming, or walking, whatever, that's great. I would say cancel it.
So look at the data. See how many times you've actually been. If you have a Fitbit or whatever, look at the last three months. Look at your bank account. See how much you actually went there. Maybe it's just a timing issue. Maybe it's just a location issue. Maybe it's just the type of exercise that you don't really enjoy. Maybe you can freeze it for two or three months and see what happens. Or maybe go to a cheaper gym. Maybe have a trainer for a month. Maybe try a different sport, a recreational sport. So try to see if there's any way to keep it before you cancel it. But if it's not working, cancel it.
I don't think canceling a gym is a bad thing. I really think that a gym membership, we should look at it like a service that we pay for. If it's helping us, I would keep it. If it's not helping us and we're just paying for guilt, I would cancel it.
